label: Dry spells
title: Longest dry spell, last 60 days
subtitle: 20 Aug to 18 Oct 2026, compared with the same days in 1991–2020 (experimental)
source: gridMET daily precipitation, averaged by parish

categories.label: About usual
categories.note: middle 40%, or within 2 days of usual

categories.label: Not rated
categories.note: too many days missing, or too few years

rank.note: Ranked by the longest dry spell in days.

how: Each parish shows its longest run of dry days (under 1 mm of rain) in the last 60 days, and whether that is longer or shorter than the same 60 days in the 30 years from 1991 to 2020. A parish is "about usual" when its longest spell is in the middle 40% of those years, or within 2 days of the usual.
limits: Experimental: this method has not been checked against the station gauges yet.
Rain is a parish average of a 4 km grid. Averaging over many cells and light drizzle in the grid shorten dry spells, so real spells at a field can be longer.
The longest spell in the window is shown, not the spell that matters for a given crop or growth stage.
A spell within 2 days of the usual is always shown as about usual, because in a short-spell parish a one-day difference moves the rank a lot and means little.
A parish is not rated when more than 10% of the window's days are missing.

credits.text: Rainfall: gridMET, Abatzoglou, J.T. (2013), Int. J. Climatology 33: 121-131
Parish boundaries: US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain)
